analyst_view.overall: Early view: Liverpool are eighth on nine points after a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahçe, their first in the league phase, and Andoni Iraola has a long injury list (Ekitike, Frimpong, Bradley, Leoni and Gravenberch with a heel fracture). Porto are 26th on three points but beat Napoli 4-1 on matchday 4 and had won 10 league games in a row at the last check. Both need the points: Liverpool to stay in the top eight, Porto to reach the play-offs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Liverpool's four league-phase games have produced 24 goals, and Porto have just scored four against Napoli. Porto's league defence has been tight (four goals against in ten games at the last check), which is the case for fewer goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.7 of them Liverpool's. I keep that: Liverpool will have more of the ball at Anfield, and Porto will defend and counter as they did against Napoli.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I see nothing to move it: neither team has a disciplinary problem in what I read, and the referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots. I lean lower: Liverpool are without several regulars (Ekitike up front, Gravenberch in midfield) and lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal in a frustrating game, while Porto under Farioli are hard to break down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I keep it: the lower shot count I expect is offset by two attacks that finish well (Isak and Wirtz for Liverpool, Samu Aghehowa and Veiga for Porto).
